title: Gap-junction coupling lets cells share sensing and form a larger Self

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Gap-junction coupling lets cells share sensing and form a larger Self

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: When cells are coupled into networks by gap junctions, the whole collective can measure and act on the same sensory data, so its Umwelt expands into a larger individual; physiological connectivity is thus the binding mechanism for larger unified Selves.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: When coupled into networks via gap junctions however, the whole collective can measure and act upon the same sensory data – the Umwelt expands to create a larger individual in which the comprising cells share a unifying picture of the world (Figure 4).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity”. Scope: Gap-junction-coupled cell networks in animal tissues

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Communication range and coordinated response are measurable in existing cell-network studies. Those observations do not uniquely establish a unified Self or gap junctions as the general binding mechanism, so the central claim is only partly resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure information transfer, shared stimulus access, and coordinated action before and after gap-junction coupling or uncoupling, and test whether coupling expands the range of stimuli that predict collective responses.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Gap junctions are not the only route for shared sensing.

A larger Self is an interpretation of increased coordination.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Shared measurement under coupling is a measurable change in the scale of a response, and the cognitive label 'larger Self' rides on that change. Public planarian atlases show where gap-junction genes are expressed, which constrains who could be coupled and does not show stimulus sharing. Functional uncoupling experiments are published as scattered physiology, not as one imaging archive. Expression data can test a proxy and leave the binding claim only partly resolved.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare the spatial scale of a response to a local stimulus in gap-junction-coupled tissue versus tissue uncoupled pharmacologically or genetically. Expansion of the responding domain while coupled, and its collapse when uncoupled, would support shared sensing; an unchanged domain would refute the physiological half of the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Common gap-junction blockers are nonspecific.

A larger responding domain can be called a larger Self or simply a larger coupled network.

Expression of innexins is not functional dye coupling or shared sensation.
